characters.name_or_role: Husband (narrator, black coat, glasses, ice cream cone)
personality_traits: Performs sincerity for a beat before revealing a joke — sets up 'real love' as if delivering a heartfelt line
Dry, deadpan comic: his mouth stays in a faint closed-lip smile/smirk through most of the monologue rather than an expressive grin, letting the absurdity of the words do the work
Self-aware about domestic routine and used to going along with his wife's forgetfulness without irritation
Relaxed and untroubled — holds a soft-serve ice cream cone the entire time, unbothered by the 'grievance' he's narrating
emotional_range: faux-profound (posing the 'real love' question with raised brows)
droll amusement (small smirk while explaining the reel-repeat premise)
performed exasperation/surprise (mouth drops open on 'Oh my god, wait!')
resigned amusement (settles back into the same smirk for 'This one too')
expressions: 0:00 eyes half-lidded, faint smile, holding up phone toward camera (as if the audience is 'seeing' something)
0:02-0:04 eyebrows raised, eyes wide, mouth slightly open — mock-serious 'ask' expression for 'you know what real love is?'
0:05-0:07 eyes relax back to half-lidded, corners of mouth curl into a small smirk during 'pretending to watch the same reel twice'
0:07-0:08 smirk holds steady, faint amusement, delivering the punchline about the wife forgetting
0:08-0:09 mouth drops open wide, eyebrows shoot up — big exaggerated surprise burst on 'Oh my god, wait!'
0:09-0:10 expression settles back to the same droll half-smile for 'This one too', mouth closing into a soft closed grin
gestures: Holds a soft-serve ice cream cone in one hand the entire scene, arm relaxed/bent at the waist, never eating it — a static prop reinforcing his laid-back mood
Head tilts slightly toward his wife when addressing the audience/her, minimal body movement, weight settled on the storefront step
No hand gestures beyond holding the cone; all emphasis is carried through face and voice, contrasting with his wife's active phone gestures
characters.interactions_notes: He is the vocal centerpiece and looks mostly toward camera/forward rather than at his wife, using her actions (scrolling, showing the phone) as the visual evidence for his verbal joke. He never breaks his passive pose to look at her directly during the punchline, suggesting the 'address' is really to the viewer, with the wife as a silent visual prop for the bit.

characters.name_or_role: Wife (tan sweater, hair bun, holding phone)
personality_traits: Cheerfully oblivious — her expression stays pleasant and slightly proud/amused while scrolling, unaware she is the butt of the joke
Active and engaged with her phone throughout, physically driving the 'plot' (the repeated reel) that her husband narrates
Warm/sociable body language (earrings, soft posture, half-smile) contrasts with the husband's flatter deadpan
emotional_range: content/absorbed (steady focus on phone screen from the first frame)
mild delighted surprise (mouth opens slightly, as if reacting to something funny on the reel)
unbothered continuation (keeps scrolling/showing phone with the same easy expression through to the end)
expressions: 0:00-0:03 eyes down at phone, soft closed-mouth smile, relaxed brow — absorbed in scrolling
0:04-0:07 eyebrows lift slightly, mouth opens a little (mid-laugh or reaction) as she shows the phone toward her husband
0:08-0:10 mouth open wider in an animated 'oh!' shape, eyes brightening — mirrors the comedic beat of 'this one too' with her own enthusiastic reaction to the phone
gestures: Holds phone with both hands at chest height for the entire scene, thumb implied scrolling motion
Tilts phone slightly toward her husband/camera at points, as if presenting the reel she's re-showing him
Torso angled toward her husband throughout, seated close beside him on the storefront step with shopping bags at her feet
characters.interactions_notes: She never makes direct sustained eye contact with her husband — her gaze stays on the phone, reinforcing the joke that she is oblivious to having shown him the same content before. He occasionally glances toward her/the phone while she looks down, so their eyelines cross but rarely lock, visually enacting the 'talking past each other but still affectionate' dynamic. Physically they sit close, shoulders nearly touching, signaling a comfortable long-term couple despite the mild ribbing.
